external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of Wellington HZ251's crash on 23 September 1943. The crew had completed a navigation exercise the previous day, landing at RAF Skipton-on-Swale due to poor weather. On departure for their home base at RAF Silloth, the aircraft took a southern route via the Irish Sea coast. Near Skipton the port wing spar failed, the wing detached, and the aircraft crashed near the Leeds-Liverpool Canal at Bridge 183.

narrative:
Wellington HZ251 of 6 (C)OTU was based at RAF Silloth, Cumbria. On 22 September 1943, the crew completed a training flight over the Pennines but were forced down by poor weather, landing overnight at RAF Skipton-on-Swale. The station operations record book records one Wellington making an unscheduled landing there that night, logging it as HE426 with the pilot as Sgt Ciaston — though the AIB accident report states it was HZ251 that diverted due to weather. The discrepancy between the two records has not been fully resolved.

On the morning of 23 September 1943, the aircraft departed Skipton-on-Swale for RAF Silloth taking a southern route via the Irish Sea coast. Near Skipton the port wing spar failed, the wing detached, and the aircraft crashed near the Leeds-Liverpool Canal at Bridge 183. All seven Polish crew were killed. F/Sgt Franciszek Ciaston PAF, aged 27, was the pilot.
